text:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: Service=redwood-inference/gpu-memory-pressure severity=high
pagerduty-bot: Trigger: GPU memory >98% on gpu-node-17 (zone: us-west2) — alert_id=PD-89321 — link: https://pd.company/alerts/PD-89321 :rotating_light:

devon: acked the PD alert and I'm on call. jumping in now.

maria: thanks — i'm the primary for this shift, devon take lead on triage, i'll own customer comms. @aj can you grab router logs?

aj: seeing a spike of OOM errors from inference-worker-42. grep'd for "CUDA out of memory" and it's repeating. sample from logs:
```
2026-04-23T14:07:02Z inference-worker-42 stderr: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512 MiB (GPU 0; 31.73 GiB total capacity; 30.98 GiB already allocated)
  File "/srv/app/serve.py", line 214, in handle_request
    result = model.generate(...)
```

aj: also noticed long-lived python processes on gpu-node-17 that look like old worker forks.

incident-bot: New incident created: I-2026-0423 — Title: GPU memory pressure on us-west2 — Severity: sev2 — Assigned: eng-oncall

support-bot: CS ticket #7890 from Acme Corp reporting degraded responses for production inference; started ~14:05 UTC. Customer-facing severity: degraded but retrying works.

devon: running quick checks: `ssh gpu-node-17 sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv`
```
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
31647 MiB, 32510 MiB
```
devon: yep almost full. `ps aux | grep python` shows several worker processes for older model versions that should have been drained. suspecting a memory leak + unfinished cleanup after rollout.

maria: can we shift traffic off gpu-node-17 to backup pool? i'd prefer graceful drain first. @liam are you available to approve an emergency fallback to the reserved pool?

liam: i'm here. approve fallback. we should enable autoscale-burst to divert new requests and then manually kill the problematic procs. estimate 15-25m.

devon: executing plan — 1) attach to node, tag worker processes, `pkill -f serve.py` for old pids 2) drain lb target for that host 3) verify memory freed 4) warm workers on replacement hosts.

aj: started a `kubectl cordon` on node gpu-node-17 and scaled down pod replica=0 for inference-deployment-old:tag-v1.2.

devon: killed stale pids: `kill -9 3412 3413 3414` — logs show those were holding large torch tensors. running `nvidia-smi` again:
```
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
1024 MiB, 32510 MiB
```
devon: memory freed, GPU usage dropped to ~1GB. starting new pods in backup pool and re-routing traffic.

maria: updating CS — Acme sees improved latency. leaving note: "We detected memory pressure on a single GPU host, drained and restarted worker processes, rerouted traffic to backup pool; monitoring for reoccurrence."

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert PD-89321 acknowledged by devon at 2026-04-23T14:09:10Z.

liam: good catch. we should build a small cleanup hook in the rollout to force worker garbage collection and ensure old worker processes are reaped. filing follow-up task after we stabilize.

sre-rotation: quick postmortem action items: 1) add metric alert for long-lived python processes on GPU nodes, 2) add pre-stop hook to inference container to free cache, 3) add PD escalation rule if same host reports >2 OOMs in 10m.

aj: monitoring for 10m. no further OOMs reported so far. logs show normal response codes and healthy tail latency.

incident-bot: Incident I-2026-0423 status changed to "monitoring" — root cause suspected: stale worker processes holding GPU memory after a partial rollout.

maria: thanks everyone — i'll keep customer updates going and i'll file the internal postmortem doc. marking this thread for follow-up with SLO impact calc. :white_check_mark:

devon: closing the immediate page. leaving runbook notes in #eng-oncall-runbooks.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: PD-89321 resolved at 2026-04-23T14:18:09Z — condition cleared.

maria: final — incident moved to postmortem; tentative timeline and notes will be in the doc. thanks all. :tada:
